title: When the Environment Gives Instructions: The Mathematics of Agent Security
outcome: Replay a fictitious attack trace against capability, provenance, and review checks.
prerequisites: The mapped chapter and its notation

input_fields.capabilities: List of permitted action names in the local contract.
input_fields.events: Ordered data/review/action events. data:instruction_attempt,promoted_to_control booleans; review:valid boolean,version; action:action,authority_source=user/system/untrusted-data,version for publish,executed boolean.

equations.label: EQV23-01
explanations: Bounds a delegated process's capability set by its parent's, so nothing reached through delegation can exceed the parent's own authority.
A child inherits at most what it is given; delegation can narrow authority, never widen it.

equations.label: EQV23-02
explanations: Advances the monitor's record from its previous state and one observed event, so authorization can be re-checked against current knowledge.
Only real, observed events move `M_t` forward; a sentence claiming an event happened is not the event.

equations.label: EQV23-03
explanations: Authorizes release only when the exact document, version, and recipient triple currently appears in the monitor's approval record.
No partial match counts: the right document at the wrong version, or the right version to the wrong recipient, both fail the lookup.

equations.label: EQV23-04
explanations: Defines exposure as the single worst violation chance across a declared attack family, not an average over the family.
One member of `\mathcal F` sets the value; a family with nine safe attacks and one dangerous one still reports the dangerous one's chance.
